Hon'ble Ajay Bhanot,J.
Matter is taken up in the revised call.

By means of this bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.153 of 2023 (S.T. No.1354 of 2023) at Police Station-Ahirauli Bazar, District -Kushinagar under Section 498A, 304B I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
The applicant is in jail since 14.08.2023.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 07.06.2024.

The following arguments made by Shri Pulak Ganguly, learned counsel assisted by Shri Ravi Bhushan, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted Shri Rakesh @ Rikesh vs State Of U.P. on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96198623/
1 Shrawan Kumar Dubey, learned AGA from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. The applicant is the husband of the deceased.
2. The applicant did not torture the deceased or demand dowry.
3. The deceased was a sensitive lady who was prone to extreme reactions even over trivial issues.
4. The deceased was depressed on account of her failure to conceive a child even after two years of marriage.
5.

sentences.text: On the fateful day, the deceased succumbed to depression and took the extreme step of ending her life.
She committed suicide by hanging.
6.The postmortem report opines the cause of death as asphyxia due to antemortem hanging.

7. Injuries depicted in the postmortem report consistent with hanging are:
(i) Nature of ligature mark.
(ii).
The hyoid bone was intact.
8. The applicant did not aid or abet the suicide.
9. The prerequisite for attracting the presumption and the reversing the burden of proof are not established in the facts and circumstances and evidence of the case.
10. Prosecution evidence does not connect the applicant with the offence.
11. The applicant works for a living in Secunderaband.

12. The applicant claims congruency in role and seeks parity in relief granted to the co-accused-Phooljhari Devi who has been granted bail by this Court on 16.01.2024 in Criminal Misc.
Bail Application No.46962 of 2023.

In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant-Rakesh @ Rikesh be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

The learned trial court is directed to fix the sureties after due application of mind in light of the judgement rendered by this Court in Arvind Singh v. State of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt.
(Application U/S 482 No.2613 of 2023).
